newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt and crown steady in calm trade.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt and crown steady in calm trade.

text.p: Sweden's debt market and the crown were flat in calm trade at midday Tuesday.
Dealers said the crown slipped back from early morning strength that was drawn from a stronger dollar and generally weakeened mark as concerns of a soft euro continued.
Dealers said the market was watching a German auction of 3.0 billion marks worth of 30-year bunds which could drive German yields higher.
"It could spill over to the Swedish market," a dealer said.
The market was also eyeing the policy making FOMC-meeting starting on Tuesday but no rate changes were expected.
The six-month T-bill rate was flat at 4.13 percent while the ten year bond yield was steady at 6.64 percent.
The crown was firmed marginally to 4.4350 crowns to the mark versus 4.4375 crowns late Monday.
It was expected to trade between 4.42 and 4.44 crowns against the mark for the rest of the day and it was likely to follow any moves in the dollar, one dealer said.
Sweden's Riksbank left its key repo rate unchanged at 4.10 pct at its weekly repurchase operation as expected.
